items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: But it's like Coleman Hawkins always was critical of Russell Smith.

ctx.x: Some people say it was because he had a strong purse, but he had a thin tone. And I always thought he had a good enough tone as a lead. The guys would play those high notes, they'd usually get a thin tone. Look at how great Cat Anderson was, or is, and his tone had to get thin when he started playing them high notes.

But it's like Coleman Hawkins always was critical of Russell Smith. He always said Fletcher (unintelligible) But everybody else always says that Russell Smith was a great lead trumpet. But Hawk always criticized him, and I think that was the reason. But that was the -- it was accurate and everything, but it was a thin sound.
